s: Jesus ascends into heaven, promising the Holy Spirit. Matthias is chosen to replace Judas.
On Pentecost the Holy Spirit comes on the apostles as tongues of fire. Peter preaches and three thousand are baptized.
Peter heals a lame man at the temple gate in the name of Jesus.
Peter and John are arrested and boldly proclaim Jesus. The believers share everything in common.
Ananias and Sapphira lie to the Spirit. The apostles are imprisoned, freed by an angel, and keep preaching.
Seven men, including Stephen, are chosen to serve the community.
Stephen recounts Israel's history, is stoned to death, and forgives his killers. Saul approves.
Persecution scatters the believers. Philip preaches in Samaria and baptizes an Ethiopian official.
The risen Jesus appears to Saul on the road to Damascus, and Saul is baptized. Peter heals Aeneas and raises Tabitha.
Peter's vision of clean and unclean animals. The Roman centurion Cornelius and his household receive the Spirit and are baptized.
Peter explains why Gentiles are welcome. At Antioch believers are first called Christians.
Herod kills James and imprisons Peter, but an angel frees him.
Barnabas and Saul are sent out on their first missionary journey.
Paul and Barnabas preach in Asia Minor, are mistaken for gods at Lystra, and Paul is stoned.
The Council of Jerusalem decides that Gentile believers need not be circumcised. Paul and Barnabas part ways.
Paul is called to Macedonia in a vision. Lydia believes at Philippi. Paul and Silas sing in prison, and the jailer is baptized.
Paul preaches in Thessalonica and Berea, and speaks of the unknown God at Athens.
Paul works as a tentmaker in Corinth with Aquila and Priscilla. Apollos preaches.
At Ephesus disciples receive the Holy Spirit. Silversmiths riot against Paul.
Paul raises Eutychus at Troas and says farewell to the elders of Ephesus.
Paul goes to Jerusalem despite warnings and is arrested in the temple.
Paul tells the crowd of his conversion.
Paul before the Sanhedrin. A plot to kill him is uncovered, and he is taken to Caesarea.
Paul defends himself before the governor Felix.
Paul appeals to Caesar before the governor Festus.
Paul tells his story to King Agrippa.
Paul sails for Rome, and the ship is wrecked in a storm, but all are saved.
Paul is welcomed on Malta and reaches Rome, where he preaches the kingdom of God openly.

1: Jesus ascends into heaven, promising to return. The apostles wait in prayer with Mary for the Holy Spirit.
2: The Holy Spirit comes on the apostles, and they begin to preach in many languages. This is the birthday of the Church.
7: Stephen dies forgiving his killers, like Jesus. A young man named Saul is watching.
9: The risen Jesus stops the persecutor Saul on the road to Damascus. Saul becomes Paul, the great apostle to the Gentiles.
10: God shows Peter that the Gospel is for everyone. The Roman Cornelius and his household are baptized.
15: The apostles and elders meet to settle a dispute. Gentile believers need not follow the law of Moses. It is the first council of the Church.
28: Paul reaches the capital of the world and preaches there freely. The Gospel has gone from Jerusalem to Rome.
